title: Some Pixel Watch 5 users are missing a Google Home feature older models already have
summary: Live view works on older Pixel Watches, making this glitch all the more puzzling.
body: TL;DR Some Pixel Watch 5 owners can’t view live camera feeds in Google Home. The feature still works on older Pixel Watches and unaffected Watch 5 units. Google’s troubleshooting steps and a replacement watch reportedly failed to resolve it. A new smartwatch shouldn’t make you miss the one it replaced. Yet barely a month into the Pixel Watch 5 ‘s life, some early owners are discovering that their older Google watches can do something the latest model cannot: show live camera feeds in the Google Home app. Several reports on Reddit and the Pixel Watch Community describe what happens when affected users select a camera in the Home app: Instead of loading the video, the watch displays a “Control more features on your phone” message and an “Open on phone” button. The feature still works normally on their older Pixel Watches.

title: Google could let Gemini punt tasks to Spark without even opening the app
summary: Using a more accessible shortcut in the floating Gemini overlay on Android.
body: Credit: Shimul Sood / Android Authority TL;DR Google could soon allow users to assign tasks to its autonomous agent, Spark, directly from the Gemini overlay. Google is also testing a similar handover feature in the main Gemini interface. The Gemini overlay could also add an option to switch models without opening the full interface. Google announced Spark , its autonomous AI agent that performs a sequence of tasks without intervention, at Google I/O 2026. Since then, Spark has rolled out in beta to Gemini (so far only to paying Google AI subscribers) on the web and mobile versions. On top of that, Google can be seen making efforts to make Spark’s skills easier to manage from mobile , especially as it looks to sunset Gems later this year . In line with those efforts, we’re now seeing evidence that Google is making it easier to assign tasks to Spark, even mid-conversation.

title: Bad Bunny Ruling, Diddy Release Date, Alanis Morissette Lawsuit & More Top Music Law News
summary: In this week's Legal Beat newsletter, Bad Bunny wins a crucial copyright decision, Diddy's date moves up, Alanis sues her ex-tour manager and much more.
body: THE BIG STORY: Bad Bunny won a major victory in the sprawling copyright lawsuit over the dembow rhythm — the boom-ch-boom-chick beat heard in nearly all reggaeton songs. The case, filed way back in 2021, has quietly grown into a behemoth with massive stakes for the music industry. Filed by reggae duo Steely & Clevie over claims that they essentially invented dembow, the lawsuit targets Bunny, Karol G , Daddy Yankee and dozens of other artists over nearly 2,000 songs that allegedly used the famous beat without permission. That would have meant years of more complex litigation, but the implications would have been even more complicated. Critics have warned that a victory for Steely & Clevie could require anyone using reggaeton’s signature beat to pay them a licensing fee, giving them an unprecedented stranglehold over an entire musical genre. But in a rare move last week, the same judge reverse…

title: Samsung takes another shot at Apple hours before iPhone Ultra/Duo launch
summary: Samsung officially welcomes Apple to the foldable segment while showing off ‘the world’s lightest fold.’
body: TL;DR Samsung’s latest ad takes a jibe at the iPhone Ultra hours ahead of the foldable’s announcement. The video highlights the Galaxy Z Fold 8 from various angles, and calls it “the world’s lightest fold.” Initial reports suggest the iPhone Ultra may cost more than the base variants of the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra. Apple’s fall hardware event is hours away, and we expect to see the company’s latest range of iPhones on show. This year, however, the manufacturer is also rumored to debut its first-ever foldable, supposedly called the iPhone Ultra or the iPhone Duo, depending on which leak you believe . One of the premier foldable brands in the business right now has, unsurprisingly, taken a subtle jab at the yet-to-be-announced foldable iPhone. In a video posted to YouTube an hour ago, Samsung formally welcomes Apple to the foldable club. While it doesn’t mention the iPhone Ultra or Apple directly, the video’s timing and title make it clear what Samsung is hinting at, though fans could argue that the company could also be welcoming users to the form factor.

title: Worried about losing Gemini Gems? Google might spare you from starting Spark Skills from scratch
summary: Google could automatically convert your Gems into Spark Skills.
body: Credit: Adamya Sharma / Android Authority TL;DR Google was previously spotted with a plan to shut down Gemini Gems in favor of Gemini Spark Skills by October 20, 2026. The latest Google app code indicates that the full shutdown of Gemini Gems has been seemingly pushed to November 17, 2026, with creation and editing privileges being disabled starting October 13, 2026. Existing Gems could also automatically convert to Gemini Spark-based Skills, saving users from having to manually recreate their setups. Google is preparing to phase out Gemini Gems and replace them with Gemini Spark -based Skills. An earlier deprecation message suggested a cut-off date of October 20, but it seems Google plans to give users some reprieve with a multi-stage timeline and a migration plan. summary: The two properties were originally slated to open in June, but those dates were pushed back to later this month.
body: The opening dates for Dolly Parton ‘s Nashville hotel and museum are just around the corner. The SongTeller Hotel and the Life of Many Colors Museum will officially open on Sept. 29, bringing to fruition two major projects the country icon was working on before her death at 80 on Aug. 25. The hotel will feature 245 guest rooms and suites, including the King rooms with expansive views of downtown Nashville and the Cumberland River, all with curated items chosen by the late Queen of Country, as well as the “Acoustic Suites,” which feature Parton’s acoustic guitars and personally curated album art and other instruments, a custom leather SongTeller journal and optional in-room songwriting sessions. title: Los Gemelos de Sinaloa Announce ‘The Gemeliza’ Album & Tour for 2026
summary: The brothers duo is beginning a new chapter after signing with Street Mob Records in April.
body: After debuting this year on the Billboard charts with their collaboration with Clave Especial and Fuerza Regida “Ferrari,” which reached No. 1 on Hot Regional Mexican Songs, Los Gemelos de Sinaloa are set to begin a new chapter alongside Street Mob Records, with a new album and tour, Billboard can exclusively announce today (Sept. 9). body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR The developer behind an unofficial GTA 5 port for Nintendo Switch is apparently working on an Android port. This unofficial GTA 5 Android port will apparently require a Snapdragon 865 chipset or newer, along with 8GB of RAM, and 65GB of storage. There’s no word on a release date, but there are a couple of reasons Grand Theft Auto 6 is scheduled to launch next month, but a developer has already unofficially ported Grand Theft Auto 5 to Nintendo Switch . title: This ‘Pro Max’ Android flagship might look very familiar, but its crazy specs steal the show
summary: Two 200MP cameras, an 8,800mAh battery, and a 500mm lens lead the charge.
body: TL;DR HONOR has revealed the Magic 9 Pro Max in Moss Green, with an iPhone Pro-like camera setup. Its dual 200MP cameras pair with optional 200mm and 500mm teleconverter lenses. An 8,800mAh battery is reportedly class-leading; the full launch follows September 28. Smartphone makers have spent years making camera bumps bigger, but HONOR’s next flagship takes that trend somewhere new — and strangely familiar. The company has officially revealed the Magic 9 Pro Max, giving us a clear look at its redesigned rear and some seriously ambitious camera hardware. Shown in a new Moss Green finish, the phone trades HONOR’s usual centered camera island for a wide plateau spanning the top of the device. A large circular module housing the flash and possibly a periscope telephoto camera sits beside two smaller lenses, with prominent ARRI branding completing the look. HONOR’s promotional images also show a contrasting rounded rectangular section immediately below the camera bar.

title: The Google Pixel 11 has an identity problem (and that’s okay)
summary: The Pixel series isn't for me, but that doesn't mean it's bad.
body: Weeks after the Google Pixel 11 launch , it’s clear the most egregious change wasn’t the price hike. The Pixel 11 Pro XL costs the same as Samsung’s Galaxy S26 Ultra, but Google could’ve justified the new price by boosting Tensor performance, doubling down on local AI features, or meaningfully changing the design. It didn’t do any of that. Google’s Tensor G6 chip is an iterative upgrade at best , my favorite Pixel exclusive uses cloud processing (Magic Capture), and the Pixel 11 Pro XL is still thicker and heavier than I’d like. To make matters worse, Google actually cut the amount of RAM on the Pro models from 16GB to 12GB.

title: End of an era: Samsung quietly ends support for Galaxy Watches that saved Wear OS
summary: The Galaxy Watch 4 and Watch 4 Classic will no longer receive any updates from Samsung.
body: Credit: Jimmy Westenberg / Android Authority TL;DR Samsung has removed the Galaxy Watch 4 and Watch 4 Classic from its Mobile Security work scope schedule, marking the end of official software and security updates. The August 2026 security patch and One UI 8 Watch update complete Samsung’s promise of four generations of Wear OS upgrades to these watches from 2021. While the smartwatches will continue to function, they will no longer receive new OS features or security patches for newly discovered vulnerabilities. It’s officially the end of the road for the Galaxy Watch 4 and Watch 4 Classic. After four generational platform upgrades culminating in the rollout of One UI 8 Watch , Samsung has now stopped security updates for these smartwatches, marking the end of an era for the wearable lineup that practically revived Google’s smartwatch ecosystem. As spotted by SamMobile , Samsung updated its Mobile Security work scope schedule following the release of its September 2026 security bulletin. Both the vanilla Galaxy Watch 4 and the physical-bezel Galaxy Watch 4 Classic have now been removed from the list of supported devices. This means the August 2026 security patch, which rolled out…

body: The latest Pixels offer plenty of improvements, from better cameras to new AI features and much more. Of course, like many newly launched devices, they aren’t without a few hiccups. Despite launching less than a month ago, the Pixel 11 has already had a small number of reported issues. As an example, our very own Joe Maring ran into issues that left his Pixel 11 Pro bricked . title: Google Keep could soon make it easier to create better, complex notes
summary: Checklists, drawings, and voice typing could soon be much easier to access.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Google is experimenting with a new pill-shaped toolbar in Keep. The toolbar makes useful editing features easier to access. However, as a result of this experiment, some other features have vanished, suggesting it may not be ready yet. “Keep it simple” is an adage that applies to Google’s default notes app, Google Keep. It’s one of the rare offerings from the tech giant that remain free of unnecessary AI additions, yet it remains incredibly useful for a variety of use cases. Rather than cramming AI features into Keep, Google is making smaller changes that make it easier to add richer elements such as checklists and different forms of media to your notes. title: The best smartphone deal in 2026 isn’t an Android phone
summary: The iPhone 17 isn’t just cheaper than Android’s latest flagships. It’s arguably the better value, too.
body: These are strange times in the smartphone world. For as long as I can remember, recommending a new smartphone was fairly simple. If you wanted a premium smartphone without spending over a thousand dollars, an Android phone was almost always the better bet. While the absolute top-end of the market remains up for debate, Samsung, Google, and a plethora of Chinese OEMs competed on price and value to make Android phones the obvious choice in that sweet $700–$800 segment. That’s no longer true.

title: Good news, bad news: Privacy Display could come to more Galaxy S27 models, but not all
summary: Don't count on Privacy Display across the board, though.
body: Credit: Stephen Radochia / Android Authority TL;DR Another source has reported that the Galaxy S27 Pro and S27 Ultra will get Privacy Display functionality. This comes a few months after we first heard that the Pro model could get Privacy Display. It sounds like this feature won’t be available on the standard and Plus models, though. The Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra debuted Privacy Display technology earlier this year. This hardware feature physically restricts viewing angles so people can’t peek at your screen. We previously heard that the rumored Galaxy S27 Pro could also get this feature, and a new leak has now corroborated this claim. ET News reports that the Galaxy S27 Pro and Galaxy S27 Ultra will both get Privacy Display functionality, citing industry sources. The outlet specifically claims that both phones will have OLED screens with Flex Magic Pixel technology. This is the hardware innovation that enables Privacy Display.

title: Motorola’s next Signature flagship could finally come to the US, official teaser hints
summary: A brief stateside appearance offers hope that this model could reach US buyers.
body: TL;DR Motorola briefly displayed an official Signature 27 teaser on its US and European websites. The pop-up showed the phone’s camera and collected emails, then abruptly disappeared. Its US appearance hints at a stateside launch, while a Swarovski edition also looks likely. Motorola only introduced the first phone in its new Signature series in January, but it already appears ready to start building anticipation for the follow-up. The company briefly teased a device called the “Signature 27” on its website — and may have shown its hand early. A Reddit user first spotted the teaser as a pop-up, and Android Authority was also able to capture the image while it was live on Motorola’s US homepage. Rather than appearing as a regular banner, it surfaced after visitors opened the site and invited them to enter their name and email address for updates.

title: Google Chat won’t lose track of your unfinished messages anymore
summary: Your half-written work messages finally have somewhere safe to hang out.
body: TL;DR Google Chat is adding persistent drafts, so unfinished messages will remain saved even if you close Chat or restart your device. Drafts will sync across devices, letting you start a message on the web and finish it later on Android or iOS. The feature is rolling out on the web now, with Android and iOS availability expected by September 28. Some work messages require a bit of thought before you hit send. You might be writing a long project update, carefully wording some feedback, or simply need to come back and finish the message later. The annoying part is putting all that thought into a Google Chat message , only to find that your unfinished text is gone when you return. Google is now fixing that with persistent drafts in Chat . Unsent messages will remain saved directly in the compose box, even if you close Chat or restart your device. So, you can leave a message halfway through, come back later, and continue exactly where you stopped.

title: Google has deployed a fix for YouTube’s blank screen problems
summary: Both YouTube and YouTube TV should now be working as normal.
body: TL;DR YouTube and YouTube TV viewers had been reporting some odd blank-screen glitches. Google earlier confirmed the issue, and offered tips for a work-around while a fix was in progress. Everything should now be back to full working order. We’re all used to dealing with the occasional glitch with the software or services we use. Maybe that takes the form of a confusing error message. Maybe it’s the app simply doing something other than what we tell it to do. But maybe the most frustrating problems of all are the kind where we just get nothing to work with — like the blank-homepage issues some YouTube users recently started reporting. That’s exactly why we’re so glad to see that Google’s already sorting this mess out. If you haven’t run into this one yourself, impacted users report firing up either YouTube or the YouTube TV app, only to see nothing much at all. With regular YouTube, thumbnails wouldn’t load, but at least we got some text. YouTube TV wasn’t even that lucky, and could just present as a fully blacked-out screen.

summary: Now Find Hub can help you locate your unconnected belongings, too.
body: Credit: Rita El Khoury / Android Authority TL;DR Find Hub’s new “Remembered” tab is starting to roll out. The new tab allows you to make a note of any object’s location. It appears the update is not widely available yet. Google recently rolled out its September Android Drop, introducing several new features to the platform. While it wasn’t available at the time, one of the new features that got announced was a new option in Find Hub designed to help you remember the locations of items that can’t be digitally tracked. The tech giant said the feature would be coming soon to devices running Android 16 or later. It seems the day for the rollout has now arrived. The folks over at 9to5Google report that Find Hub’s new “Remembered” tab is here. It will join Devices and People as the third available option on the bottom bar. It is marked by a bookmark icon with a Gemini spark in the top right corner.

title: Missing Nest alerts on your iPhone? Google’s got a fix
summary: Google resolves issues with missing Nest alerts on iOS devices.
body: TL;DR For the past few days, iPhone users have reported not getting Nest camera alerts on their devices. While the app still recorded events, notifications for them weren’t going through. Google shares that this glitch should now be resolved. A good smart home demands openness: With as many different devices as you’ll need to really get every last corner of your home automated, it’s critical that they all play nicely with each other. For Google Home , part of that means not arbitrarily setting up platform boundaries, and Google’s smart home solution is open for Apple users to enjoy. Unfortunately, Nest devices in particular have been experiencing a few hiccups lately when it comes to iOS devices — but Google’s already got good news. We expect a few key features from any smart home setup — it needs to provide remote control through our devices, it should support automated actions, and it should notify us about things worth our attention. With Nest on iOS, however, users have reported running into trouble with that last one, sharing on sites like Reddit the problems they recently noticed with Nest notifications not coming through on iOS devices .

title: Samsung flexes its foldable lead one day before Apple joins the race
summary: The lineup is attracting a lot more first-time foldable buyers than ever before.
body: TL;DR Combined US purchases of the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Fold 8 Ultra are tracking 30% ahead of the Galaxy Z Fold 7. The two Fold models account for roughly 80% of current Galaxy Z8 series purchases in the US. Samsung says 30% of Galaxy Z Flip 8 buyers switched from competing brands, with most buying their first foldable. Apple’s big hardware event is scheduled for tomorrow, September 9, and the Cupertino-based company is finally expected to unveil a new device category that competitors like Samsung have spent years mastering: foldables. However, before the tech giant gets to enter the foldable market, Samsung is sharing figures to highlight just how much of a head start it’s working with. Roughly a month after launching the Z Flip 8, Z Fold 8 Ultra, and the all-new wide Z Fold 8, Samsung is highlighting how the lineup is changing foldable preferences in the US.

title: Google is leveling up Sheets with dozens of new fonts
summary: The update also improves font compatibility between Sheets and Excel.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR Google Sheets now supports the full Google Fonts web font library. This font update also enhances import and export capabilities between Sheets and Excel. The rollout is available to all Workspace customers and personal Google accounts. Last month, Google rolled out a Sheets update that preserves formatting and structural information when importing Excel files. Google is now taking another step toward further improving importing and exporting between the two apps. Best of all, you won’t have to wait long for it to arrive. The latest Google Sheets update expands the number of font options that will be available to you. According to the announcement , the company’s spreadsheet app will now support the full Google Fonts web font library. This expanded support will be available for chart titles and subtitles, horizontal and vertical axis titles and labels, data labels, and legend text.

title: Google Maps on Android Auto finally got this highly requested feature, but now it’s disappearing
summary: Did the speedometer and speed limit indicator also disappear for you?
body: Credit: C. Scott Brown / Android Authority TL;DR Android Auto users are reporting an issue with Google Maps. The affected users say that they can no longer see the speedometer and speed limit indicator. Some users say that stop signs and traffic signals have disappeared, too. Waze users on Android Auto are currently experiencing a bug that’s hiding their journey information . However, Waze isn’t the only navigation app having technical difficulties at the moment. It appears that Google Maps is also having trouble on the platform. The issue concerns a feature that recently started rolling out for the app on Android Auto. Google Maps on mobile has long had a live speedometer feature. The feature is even available in Google Maps on Apple’s CarPlay experience. However, Google didn’t get around to adding this feature to Android Auto until recently. The first reports of the live speedometer arriving on Android Auto started in July , when it rolled out to select Maps beta testers.

The repetition occurred despite having Spotify’s “Fewer Repeats” toggle switched on and without changing devices or playlists. The findings suggest Spotify could be either aggressively caching queues or reusing shuffle seeds rather than properly re-randomizing playlists. If you have ever felt like Spotify’s shuffle feature is just cycling through the same handful of tracks on repeat, you are certainly not alone. Users have spent years venting their frustrations about Spotify’s shuffle algorithm , frequently questioning whether the system is truly randomized or simply running your favorites through an endless echo chamber. While listener complaints are usually dismissed as mere confirmation bias, one user went down a data rabbit hole to prove that the music streaming giant’s playback queue might actually be serving up exact clones of previously heard playlists. title: Google Search is being forced to change, and some users might feel the pinch
summary: Google is (reluctantly) rewriting how Search works for some users.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR Google is being forced to change how Search works in the European Union (EU). These changes will allow results from rival vertical search services (like Expedia or Booking.com) to appear before Google’s own. Google says these changes will degrade the experience for European users. After the European Union recently imposed a $1 billion fine on Google for allegedly violating the Digital Markets Act (DMA), Google is changing how Search works in the region. This changes how Google search results appear in EU countries, which, the company’s representatives say, could deteriorate the quality of results for people in the region. Earlier today, Google confirmed to Reuters that it was implementing “significant changes to Search in Europe.” The changes appear to apply particularly when users search for services such as flights or hotels (also known as vertical search services or VSS), where Google will now be required to show results from its top competitors before serving its own Flights, Hotels, or other services.

title: Snapseed leans harder into professional editing with color grading and other upcoming features
summary: We’re also getting our first glimpse at the reorganized Looks menu in Snapseed.
body: TL;DR Snapseed has rolled out a new update for Android, introducing features like a color grading tool and a dedicated search bar. The app has also replaced the previous googly-eyed loading animation with a leaf fan spinner. These features are currently live for everyone, but we’ve found that Snapseed is also working on a complete overhaul of a key menu. The Snapseed app for Android saw its biggest update in a couple of years this May , following a long wait behind iOS users. Since then, we’ve found that the Google-run app still has more changes in progress, such as the color grading tool we exclusively reported on in July. This tool is now rolling out to everyone, along with a couple of other inclusions. Snapseed’s latest version 4.1.6 update now includes the Color Grade tool by default among the list of tools. While the tools menu is set to All by default, Color Grade is also in the Refine submenu. This tool lets users modify a photo’s tones and colors to achieve a specific art style.
